clue.text: Making one on scoring

definitions.meaning: reads like chalking up a point or adding one to a tally in a game
in slang, scoring is succeeding in having sex with someone

explanation.surface: A sports commentator notes a team pulling a goal back.
explanation.walkthrough: GETTING ONE'S END AWAY is British slang for having sex; the clue dresses the act up as putting a point on the scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the slang phrase and the slang verb mean achieving sexual intercourse with someone.

clue.text: Got hold of "large sum of money found on ex-Conservative minister" plot

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another means it comes first

parts.note: G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds
Rab Butler was a senior Conservative minister of the 1950s and 60s
a bed is a plot in a garden, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline on a scandal of a big payment to a former Tory minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot looks like a conspiracy to go with the scandal, but it is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab something is to seize it, so grabbed means took hold of in the past tense.

clue.text: Singer — fantastic big tits, old boy — sacrificing Scala opening for love

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly reshaped, so the letters are scrambled
with for, gives up one letter and puts another in its place
with sacrificing, names the letter that comes in

parts.note: taken as written
OB is the abbreviation for an old boy of a school

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word Scala

parts.note: taken as written; its first letter is the one given up
love is nil in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A busty singer gives up her La Scala debut for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala is Milan's opera house, apt for the Italian baritone Tito Gobbi.
explanation.definitionFit: Tito Gobbi was a celebrated Italian operatic baritone, so he is an example of a vocalist.

clue.text: They're supposed to sexually abuse kippers

definitions.meaning: legend has these demons lie on women in their sleep
smoked herrings on the surface; here people having a kip, a British word for a nap

explanation.surface: An absurd claim that someone molests smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A kip is British slang for a sleep, so kippers are sleepers; 'supposed' marks the demons as mythical.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are male demons of folklore believed to have sex with sleeping women.

clue.text: No expert, Olive, when it comes to an erection

parts.note: olive is a shade of green
horn is British slang for an erection

explanation.surface: Popeye's Olive Oyl is a novice when it comes to sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive looks like a woman's name; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, a novice rather than a practised hand.

clue.text: Saw off bollocks before producing laughs

parts.note: British slang for nonsense, as is guff

indicators.note: something gone off is spoilt or out of order, so the letters of saw are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone castrates with a saw and the onlookers fall about laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw off bollocks' reads as a gruesome act; bollocks is really the noun meaning rubbish, and off works on saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Guffaws are loud hearty bursts of laughter, so the plural noun matches laughs.

clue.text: Stupid, cloyingly sentimental material by gutless Weldon

parts.note: goo is sickly sentimentality

indicators.note: with its insides removed, so just the outer letters of the name remain

parts.note: Fay Weldon was a British novelist

explanation.surface: A sneer at Fay Weldon's novels as gooey sentimental rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Weldon gives the novelist's first name, Fay, not her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Goofy means silly or foolish, an informal synonym for daft.

clue.text: You'd hardly be aware of such a slip if under a shift

definitions.text: You'd hardly be aware of such a slip

indicators.note: shifted letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman wearing a slip under a shift dress would barely notice it.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip and shift are both women's undergarments or dresses on the surface; shift is really the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freudian slip is an error said to reveal an unconscious wish, so the speaker is barely aware of it.

clue.text: See you go down in gold

indicators.note: says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to die is to go down, as a ship or a fallen fighter does

explanation.surface: A farewell to someone sinking amid riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell used in English, a goodbye like see you.

clue.text: "Live in sin" journalist into drink

indicators.note: puts the journalist inside the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
a hack is a journalist, often a disparaging term

explanation.surface: A boozy reporter moves in with a lover out of wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: To shack up is to live together as a couple without marrying, the old phrase living in sin.

clue.text: Putting sex back into political party is an odd thing to do

indicators.note: together with into, says one piece is placed inside another
with Putting, says the reversed sex goes inside the party

parts.note: the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

indicators.note: read backwards, so the word for sex is turned round

parts.note: IT is the old euphemism for sex appeal or sex itself

explanation.surface: A satirical jab: injecting sex into politics is a strange move for a party to make.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a ludicrous or grotesque act, a piece of strange behaviour or capering.

clue.text: Piss artist found in the middle of Ted Heath's secret stuff

indicators.note: says the drunk sits inside the other letters
takes just the central letter of the name Ted

parts.note: the name Ted, whose central letter is all that is used
Erica is the botanical genus of heath and heather
British slang for a heavy drinker, a sot

explanation.surface: Gossip that a drunk lurks within former Prime Minister Ted Heath's hidden papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath looks like one name for the former Tory Prime Minister, but it splits: Ted for its middle letter, heath for the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are things understood only by an inner circle, so arcane or private material.

clue.text: Animated film star puts listening device in hostess's cleavage?

parts.note: to bug something is to plant a hidden microphone in it
a Bunny was a hostess at a Playboy Club; her cleavage is just where the bug is hidden

explanation.surface: A spy plants a microphone down a nightclub hostess's front.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'bugs bunny' is read literally as bugging a Playboy Bunny.
explanation.definitionFit: The Warner Bros cartoon rabbit is one of the most famous characters in animation.

clue.text: Take dip without resistance, being pissed

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the dip wraps round the resistance

parts.note: to dunk is to dip, as a biscuit into tea
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone sloshed takes a plunge into the water without hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, which would remove letters; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pissed is British slang for intoxicated, and drunk is the plain word for the same state.

clue.text: Roger turned out finally to be a liability

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for sex is read backwards

parts.note: to roger is British slang for having sex, as is to bed someone

indicators.note: takes just the closing letter of out

parts.note: the word out, whose last letter is all that is used

explanation.surface: A man called Roger proved to be more trouble than he was worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger looks like a man's name; here it is the slang verb, matched by bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, which accountants list among liabilities.

clue.text: Southern batter preceded by fish balls

indicators.note: puts the fish in front of the southern batter

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
to wallop is to hit hard, to batter

explanation.surface: A chip-shop order: southern-style batter with fish balls in front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Batter and fish suggest a fish supper, but batter is the verb to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is British slang for nonsense, and codswallop is a jocular word for utter rubbish.

clue.text: Underwear attachment for a swinger

definitions.meaning: a strap holding up a stocking, attached to a belt
a person who swaps sexual partners, and also anything that swings from a support

explanation.surface: Lingerie to suit a sexually adventurous partner-swapper.
explanation.walkthrough: Something that hangs and swings is suspended, so a swinger needs one to hang from.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment strap and the thing that hangs something up share the same name.

clue.text: Ken's sort of people: unsociable types, academic at heart

indicators.note: says the academic is set in the centre of the other word

parts.note: loners keep to themselves
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A dig at Ken's associates as antisocial bookish oddballs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is Ken Livingstone, Mayor of London when this ran.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayor of London's constituents are the capital's residents, the people he represents.

clue.text: To a Scot, a good man will show way to mount a royal

definitions.text: To a Scot, a good man

indicators.note: in a down clue, the street climbs on top of the royal and so comes first

parts.note: Prince Andrew, son of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A Scot says a worthy man will demonstrate how to get on top of a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good man' is a saint, and Andrew is Scotland's patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland, a holy man revered by Scots.

clue.text: Being pissed off and other siren's shit

indicators.note: asks for a different arrangement of the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up, and so is everyone else, with a seductress's rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Pissed off here is British for annoyed, not drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirty is British slang for bad-tempered, so shirtiness is the state of being annoyed.

clue.text: Very lewd beginning then awfully blue — just what this crossword should be

definitions.text: just what this crossword should be

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of lewd

parts.note: the word lewd, whose first letter is all that is used

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude, filthy-from-the-off puzzle is exactly what Private Eye's Cyclops promises.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies the crossword should be smutty; the definition says it should be solvable.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle you can work out is solvable, and soluble is the standard word for that.

clue.text: See 1
Sex appeal, to a churchman holding an amusing organ, is looking forlorn

parts.note: SA is the old abbreviation for sex appeal

indicators.note: the churchman holds the organ inside him

parts.note: a DD is a Doctor of Divinity
the eye, and a nod to Private Eye, the satirical magazine running this puzzle

explanation.surface: A clergyman's dismal charms are spoilt by an organ that makes people laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ suggests a church instrument, or something ruder; it is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad-eyed describes a mournful expression, so it suits someone looking miserable.

clue.text: Wear a shawl and shut your face!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put on warm layers
second meaning: slang for be quiet

explanation.walkthrough: The shawl suggests a granny being told to pipe down, but the two halves are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both dressing warmly and, as a command, telling someone to stop talking.

clue.text: Spill the beans about not entirely honourable Tony

indicators.note: says only part of the phrase that follows is used, the answer lying inside it

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of honourable and the start of Tony holds the answer

explanation.surface: Revealing secrets about a less than honourable Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to reveal a secret, informally the same as spilling the beans.

clue.text: Cyclops enters a bit overcome

indicators.note: the setter goes inside the small amount

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
the setter's pseudonym, so the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter walks in and is somewhat overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is this puzzle's setter, so naming himself gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tamed has been subdued or brought under control, that is, overcome.

clue.text: Bugger Saturday clothing pledge

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for Saturday in timetables
wear is clothing, as in menswear
your word is a promise, as in giving your word

explanation.surface: Someone curses as they make a solemn vow about what to wear on Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: Bugger reads as an exclamation starting the sentence, which is exactly what it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugger is a classic British expletive, an example of a profanity or oath.

clue.text: Brazen like the salsa?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: covered in or like sauce, salsa being a spicy sauce

explanation.walkthrough: Salsa looks like the sexy dance, but it is the sauce; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both cheeky and impudent, and literally sauce-like or full of sauce.

clue.text: Arse (drinks enough for the whole group) producing loaf

parts.note: British slang for backside, as is bum

parts.words: drinks enough for the whole group
parts.note: a round is one set of drinks bought for everyone at the table, here a round

explanation.surface: A drinking session leaves somebody's backside fit only to loll.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf looks like bread; it is the verb meaning to idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum around is to idle or drift about doing nothing, the same as to loaf.

clue.text: Tart, model, wants head from your Holiness

parts.note: a tart is a type of pie
the Model T was Ford's famous car

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word your

parts.note: the word your, whose first letter is all that is used

explanation.surface: A tart and a model each petition the Pope for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Your Holiness reads as addressing the Pope; Holiness is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is devoutness and religious reverence, close in sense to holiness or saintliness.

clue.text: See 1
Slept about and showed off body

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about, as in a letter heading
to pose is to display your body, as a model does

explanation.surface: Someone slept around and then flaunted their physique.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to rest or lie asleep, so reposed matches slept in the past tense.
